cycles.method: measured under ot_emu --mkii (the ColdFire port; emulator, not hardware), executed ColdFire instructions from the YES press to the toast, not chip cycles: 11,083,553 for the blend at fader 64 with every scene byte of all eight tracks locked in both scenes (231 writes; frame engine on, so interrupt instructions in that window are included; perf bound.py, 20 Oct 2026); 8,268,075 for verify.py's worst case (201 writes, frame engine off). No static bound: the per-write cost is stock's page-1 writer 0x40054cd8, which took 76 to 1,404,162 instructions per write in that one apply, depending on the parameter; nothing in this repository bounds it. Budget: 100 ms at 266 MHz, a key-press responsiveness target, not a measured limit.

load.method: Emulator, not hardware: ot_emu --mkii --dsp (the ColdFire port, built from the upstream:tools Octabam checkout 67e5ea37), 20 Oct 2026. Two native static-stock images from this source: CF METER + CF METER IDLE + the stock effects (upstream Octabam's probe, private, not in Modwerk), and the same plus APPLY SCENE; the same project (verify.py's fixture with T8 FX2 = CF METER, every scene byte of all eight tracks locked in both scenes except T8's FX2 page), transport playing, crossfader 64, 10 s of the same MIDI flood on both (one three-byte message per ms: notes on and off and CCs on channels 1-8 and 11, about 1,000 a second, plus clock at 240 BPM), and the same panel presses on both: SCENE A, SCENE B and both + YES about every 0.65 s (16 applies on the APPLY SCENE image). Longest frame interrupt: the largest per-cycle 'isr max' that tools/harness/cfmeter.py --dump (upstream Octabam's decoder) reads from five 2 s cycles, in the port's own time (it prices each instruction at one step, so these microseconds are not the unit's). Idle: CF METER IDLE reads 0 % on both images because the port fast-forwards main's idle park, so idle is the port's own share instead: 100 x (1 - executed instructions / (3,990 instructions per sample x elapsed samples)) over the run. The same flood without presses: longest 129.3 us stock, 129.1 us APPLY SCENE, idle 62.4 % both (the module costs nothing between presses). During the presses the longest interrupt rises to 135.9 us (stock with the same presses: 129.0 us) and idle falls by 3.7 points.

stress.droppedExplanation: Emulator, not hardware: ot_emu --mkii --dsp, the APPLY SCENE image and project above, 62 s of the flood (62,098 three-byte messages and 5,963 clocks), transport playing; at 7, 22, 37 and 52 s STOP with a note held on channel 1, then Part 2, PLAY and Part 1 (the Part changed by calling stock's own selection routine 0x4004a8a4, because PART + TRIG did not change it in the port's panel script); SCENE A, SCENE B or both + YES every 5 s (11 applies, up to 6,832,603 instructions each). Dropped: counted at the MIDI thread's handlers (note on, note off, CC, clock, start, stop, docs/firmware/MIDI.md); every type's handler entries were at least the messages sent (one or two more entries than sent on some types, in the stock run too: the PC watch counting an entry twice, not extra input), and none were missing. Stuck notes: every note-on had its note-off dispatched, nothing was sent to MIDI OUT, and the firmware's per-channel note bookkeeping at the end is identical to the stock image's under the same input; no samples are loaded and no MIDI track plays notes in this project, so audible stuck notes could not occur here. Hangs: frames advanced to the end and a SCENE A + YES after the final STOP was answered. Bypass and MIDI channel changes do not apply: the module has no bypass and no MIDI path.

hardwareEvidence.note: The MKII run (15 Oct 2026, the USB package of ae2a6eed) was functional only: values watched on the screen, nothing timed or recorded. The load and stress rows above are ot_emu measurements; docs/MODULE_QUALIFICATION.md does not count emulator-only evidence as qualification. The cycles row has no static bound.
